meta.sub: Scored from source: a shallow clone of github.com/treeverse/lakeFS at 4bb11638 (2026-08-16), read by a 14-agent pass — 5 subsystem recon readers, 4 dimension scorers, 4 adversarial verifiers demanding file:line evidence, 1 comparison critic. Reconciliation: misconfig lowered by a verifier, CAS raised and upgrades trimmed by the critic, failure shape lowered 4→3 in post-publication review. One column, two postures — server API/gateway cells vs lakectl-local cells (each note says which face earns what). Everest mount (NFS/FUSE) is enterprise and absent from this repo.

notes.Consistency: lakeFS replaced the filesystem with a KV-CAS commit store: acked writes are already in S3 + KV before the app sees success (4.5 vs Lean 1.5, graveler staging), API readers see staged writes immediately, and branch/merge machinery arbitrates with per-key conflict refusal (graveler.go:2289). The filesystem axes invert — no locks, no rename anywhere in the API, no shared sqlite/git — and foreign S3 writes are the mirror of Lean’s inbox: hidden, served corrupt under a stale ETag, or GC-deleted (1 vs 4). CAS raised 3.5→4 by the critic: refusal-grade KV insert-if-absent outweighs the missing object-level If-Match.
notes.Performance: An envelope of two postures no single workload gets at once: hot-loop 5 and cold start belong to lakectl-local checkouts (plain files, nothing on the I/O path), while metadata-heavy work pays 2–3 HTTPS round-trips per file (2.5 vs Lean’s 5). Streaming rides presigned-direct to S3; scale-out is stateless replicas until the KV store binds (4). Envelope 2.5: every POSIX workload needs a full local copy the repo’s own CLI warns is non-scalable.
notes.Security: The score rests on SigV4 per-request signing at the gateway plus presigned URLs keeping bucket credentials server-side — OIDC/SAML/RBAC are enterprise (pkg/auth/build.go Fatals non-basic modes), so shipped OSS is effectively one superAdmin: tenancy 1.5 is where the split bites. Misconfig lowered 3→2.5 by the verifier: blockstore.signing.secret_key defaults to a publicly-known constant in ALL modes (config/defaults.go:107). Default-on hooks put writer-authored webhooks on the server’s network position.
notes.Day-2 operations: Cheapest fleet citizen per share: a parked repo is KV rows plus bytes (idle 4.5), consumers need only a CLI/SDK (4.5), rolls are stateless restarts. Failure shape lowered 4→3 on review: server/KV death stops the whole data plane for every API/gateway consumer fleet-wide — only lakectl-local working files ride it out — where Lean’s running pods keep serving. And the axes don’t price the structural contrast: Lean operates ZERO databases (the bucket is the DR story); lakeFS carries an operated KV (refs + all uncommitted staging) plus an external Spark GC job. Observability 2.5: no per-repo metrics dimension; /_health checks neither KV nor blockstore.

headlines: lakeFS beats Lean exactly where the server owns the truth — an acked write is already in S3 plus the KV store before the app sees success (4.5 vs 1.5), API readers see each other’s staged writes immediately (3.5 vs 1.5), and branch/merge machinery genuinely arbitrates concurrent writers with per-key conflict refusal (3.5 vs 2.5). The structural reason: it replaced the filesystem with a commit store.

Everything filesystem-shaped inverts. No locks, no rename, no shared sqlite/git across clients (1.5); metadata storms pay HTTPS round-trips against Lean’s local-NVMe 5; every POSIX workload needs a full local checkout. The mount that would fix this — Everest, NFS/FUSE write mode — is enterprise and not in this codebase.

On out-of-band writes the two systems are exact mirrors: Lean preserves and surfaces foreign S3 writes through its inbox (4); lakeFS hides them, schedules them for GC deletion, or serves a foreign overwrite corrupt under an unverified stored ETag (1). The object store is lakeFS’s private heap, not a shared surface.

As a fleet citizen lakeFS is cheaper than Lean per share — parking is free, consumers featherweight, rolls stateless — but it concentrates what Lean distributes: server/KV death stops the whole API data plane fleet-wide (failure shape 3 vs 3.5), OSS multi-tenancy is one superAdmin (tenancy 1.5 vs 4), and the default-on hooks engine puts writer-authored synchronous webhooks inside the commit path (pkg/actions, 6.4k LOC — flagged by the critic from a subsystem no scorer had read).
foot: Method: recon → score → adversarial verify (file:line evidence, 452 tool calls) → cross-dimension critique; reconciliation adopted the verifier’s misconfig adjustment and the critic’s CAS raise, upgrades trim, and two-postures caveat. Evidence basis differs from pages 1–3: the flint columns are doc-grounded and drill-proven; this column is code-inferred from one commit (4bb11638) of the OSS repo — Everest mount, RBAC, and OIDC/SAML are enterprise deltas noted per cell. Radar overlays show Lean vs lakeFS; the tables carry every column. Post-publication review lowered Day-2 failure shape 4→3: the two-postures envelope had credited the API/gateway face with lakectl-local’s outage behavior.
